key_insight: A tabular foundation model can perform pre-fault dynamic security assessment for many power-system contingencies via in-context learning, reducing the need for per-contingency retraining and large labeled datasets.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more scalable stability screening in power-system operations, including better handling of previously unseen contingencies with only a few new labels.
method: Uses a tabular foundation model (TFM) instead of one classifier per contingency
Applies in-context learning with no retraining or hyperparameter tuning
Tests electrical distance coordinates (EDC) as continuous features to support transfer to unseen contingencies
evidence_signal: On the IEEE 68-bus system, the approach achieved about 90% average Macro F1 with only 120 labeled samples per contingency, and 10 labeled samples for a new contingency with EDC matched the best transfer-learning oracle.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen contingencies depends on feature encoding, so EDC may not help in all cases and a small labeled set may still be needed.
paper_title: Revisiting data-driven dynamic security assessment with a tabular foundation model
